description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (in percent) of four different video understanding models as a function of the number of frames, evaluated on the EgoSchema dataset for length extrapolation. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Frames,” spans from approximately 5 to 65 frames, with major tick marks at intervals of 10. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy (%)”, ranges from 39% to 55%, with major gridlines and tick labels at 1% intervals. Four distinct lines are plotted: “Ours (Dynamic Seg)” (blue line with circular markers) starts near 53% at 5 frames, rises to ~54% by 15 frames, and remains stable near 54% up to 65 frames. “Ours (Static 4-Seg)” (green line with circular markers) begins at ~52.5% at 5 frames, increases to ~53.8% by 15 frames, and plateaus near 54% through 65 frames. “PLLaVA (DP 8)” (orange line with square markers) starts at ~45% at 5 frames, declines steadily to ~43% at 15 frames, ~41% at 30 frames, and reaches ~39.5% at 65 frames. “PLLaVA (DP 16)” (red line with square markers) begins at ~45.5% at 5 frames, drops to ~44% at 30 frames, and continues decreasing to ~42% at 65 frames. All lines show that the “Ours” methods maintain high and stable accuracy across frame counts, while both PLLaVA variants exhibit a consistent decline in accuracy as the number of frames increases.
